To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have derived filters that estimate the parameters of a hidden Markov model (HMM) and a sinusoidal model (SM) with a mixture of Gaussian noise and deterministic signal, and that we have used the filters in a filtered EM algorithm for maximum likelihood estimation of the HMM and SM parameters.

(1) a filtered EM algorithm for the joint estimation of the Markover parameters and the parameters of the sinusoidal signals is derived, and (2) the filtered EM algorithm is computationally efficient in comparison to the smoothed EM algorithm.

(i) the proposed algorithm is a significant advance over the state-of-the-art, in that it is the only one that is capable of jointly estimating Markov chain parameters and sinusoidal parameters, and (ii) the proposed algorithm provides a computationally efficient solution to this problem, in that it requires only a fraction of the memory required by the state-of-the art algorithm, and it has the potential for parallel processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the parameters of hidden Markov models and the parameters of deterministic signals in the presence of Gaussian white noise.
the problem of estimation of the parameters of discrete-valued time series with a known structure.
the development of a class of filters for estimating the state of a hidden Markov chain in the presence of deterministic signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed filter-based EM algorithm provides a practical and effective alternative to the forward-backward EM algorithm in many applications.
the filter-based EM algorithm is a viable alternative to the smoothed-variable EM algorithm, especially in situations where memory is limited and/or the number of observations is large.
the proposed algorithm provides a computationally efficient alternative to the standard EM algorithm for the estimation of Markov chain parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is an EM-based algorithm that is able to estimate the parameters of both the hidden Markov model (HMM) and the deterministic signals.
we have proposed a new approach to the estimation of the parameters in a joint hidden Markov and sinusoidal parameter model, which is based on the use of finite-dimensional filters.
we have developed an algorithm that is able to track the parameters of a hidden Markov model that generates a signal with sinusoidal interference and polynomial drift.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EM algorithm can be implemented in a computationally efficient manner for joint estimation of hidden Markov models and deterministic signals.
we show how to use the EM algorithm to estimate the hidden Markov model parameters and sinusoidal parameters in a computationally tractable way.
the EM algorithm is not just an iterative algorithm that requires a large number of iterations to converge.
